headline: Unpatched Tailscale SSH flaws reported; VeloCloud and Collabora KEV deadline is tomorrow; LiteLLM 1.107.0 and PHP2Shell still active

bullets.text: New since the last SITREP: The Hacker News reports unpatched flaws in Tailscale SSH that could let a hacked device on a tailnet reach root on other servers. No fix is named yet.

CISA's Oct 26 deadline is tomorrow for exploited SQL injection in Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator (CVE-2026-114625), its third zero-day in four months, and OS command injection in Collabora Online's CODE server (CVE-2026-110447).

LiteLLM: a leaked master key let attackers steal GitHub tokens and hijack the release pipeline. Microsoft's analysis shows version 1.107.0 on PyPI and Docker stole credentials through Python startup hooks.

PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) allows unauthenticated code execution; fixes are in 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. Exploit attempts hit millions of hosts, some deploying Mirai. A third bug, CVE-2026-115560, will not get an emergency fix.

Railway is telling all users to rotate secrets after a potential breach. Ruby fixed three regex engine bugs behind four critical GitLab RCE flaws, and Pillow has a FlashPix heap overflow allowing code execution from a crafted image.

Breaches confirmed: Quest Diagnostics patient personal and health data, 11.7 million CAPCOM ID accounts, and over 70,000 firewall and VPN credentials. Microsoft 365 accounts at 79 organizations were taken over with stolen sessions.

actions: Before tomorrow's deadline: patch or take offline Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator and Collabora Online (CODE server), and check both for compromise.
If you use Tailscale SSH, tighten ACLs so only trusted devices can SSH to servers, and watch for Tailscale's fix.
Search lockfiles, images and CI caches for litellm 1.107.0. If it ever ran, treat the host as compromised and rotate every credential it could read.
Update PHP to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35, rebuild images that bundle PHP, and restart PHP-FPM or Apache.
Review Microsoft 365 sign-ins for session reuse and revoke suspicious sessions; if you deploy on Railway, rotate every secret stored there.
Patch self-managed GitLab and update Ruby and Pillow in your apps and images.
